Subject: Quick follow-up + recap from today's call — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Thanks again for taking the time today, Jared — really helpful conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same playbook: 

Recap:
- Primary constraint: data isolation and control over encryption keys for inference inputs/outputs and diagnostic logs.
- Secondary constraints: SOC 2 evidence, network egress restrictions, and the ability to retain logs in your cloud account for forensics.
- You're evaluating two options with us: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity in Redwood-managed infra) vs Redwood Private (customer VPC or on-prem package).

Key clarifying questions we need from your side to recommend a path: 
1) Is it a hard requirement that no customer data or logs may leave your VPC/account?
2) Do you require customer-managed KMS/HSM for model request encryption (BYOK)?
3) Who on your network/security team can we engage for a short technical session (firewall rules, CIDR ranges, peering/VPN)?

What we propose next: 
- Marissa (cc'd) to run a technical deep dive next week to map the network/KMS options for both Dedicated and Private.
- I'll share a short comparison doc + SOW draft for the two options.
- If Private VPC is required, we'll schedule an architecture call with your infra team to scope the VPC deployment and KMS integration.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-faq.pdf (short FAQ), SOW-draft-v1.docx (initial scope).

Next steps / ask for you: reply with answers to the 3 questions above and availability for a 60-min technical call (we suggested Tue/Wed next week).

Thanks — Mateo

Thanks, Mateo — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Hard requirement: inference inputs/outputs and any raw logs must not leave our cloud account unless we explicitly opt-in. We need to own retention and deletion.
2) KMS: We need BYOK; keys must be in our AWS account (HSM is a plus).
3) Network contact: that's Anika (cc). She can own network/peering questions.

Also attaching our security checklist (FinSecure_security_checklist.xlsx) — it has a few items you'll probably want a heads-up on (certs, endpoint auth methods, and log access patterns).

Question for you: with Dedicated, is it possible to route all telemetry/logs to a customer-owned S3 or CloudWatch in our account? If not, we'd need Private VPC.

Availability: Tue 10–12 PT or Wed 2–4 PT works for us.

Cheers,
Jared

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + recap from today's call — Dedicated vs Private VPC

Appreciate the quick reply and the checklist, Jared. Short answers and proposed next steps: 

Short answers: 
- Dedicated: provides tenant isolation and reserved GPU pools in Redwood's environment. Logs/telemetry are by default stored in Redwood's account, but we have integrations that can forward structured telemetry. Full customer-owned log storage and BYOK are not standard on Dedicated; they require additional controls and an elevated security engagement.
- Private VPC: built for exactly this case — private control plane + deployment inside your VPC (or our on-prem option). With Private VPC we can support BYOK (your KMS/HSM) and keep inference logs and artifacts in your account; network egress is controllable by your security team.

Given your answers, it sounds like Private VPC is the safer default recommendation. That said, some customers choose Dedicated with an enterprise security addendum and custom routing if they have looser requirements — but that typically involves a longer compliance/legal process.

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa to run a technical deep dive and produce a checklist of exact network/KMS items we need from FinSecure.
- I'll send an updated SOW that includes Private VPC pricing and a timeline for a POC.
- Proposed tech call: Tue 10:30–11:30 PT (matches your availability). Marissa, can you confirm?

Please let us know if you want us to prioritize an on-prem scoping instead of VPC — we can include that in the SOW.

Thanks — Mateo
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Hi Jared / team — thanks for the checklist. I'm happy to run the technical deep dive tomorrow. Short technical notes / what we'll need from you to scope Private VPC fully: 

Required from FinSecure for Private VPC scoping:
- Primary cloud provider and account IDs (AWS account number).
- Target VPC CIDR(s), preferred subnets for peering, and any existing Transit/VPN details.
- KMS key ARN(s) for BYOK or HSM vendor details (if applicable).
- Desired retention window for inference request/response logs and where you want them stored (S3 bucket ARN, CloudWatch).
- Any IP allowlist or egress-deny requirements (we need to validate whether Redwood control plane access will be allowed from your VPC).

Security artifacts we can share immediately:
- SOC 2 Type II summary + scope (pdf).
- Network architecture template for the Private VPC deployment (attached: redwood-private-vpc-faq.pdf has the high-level).

Proposed next steps and timeline:
1) Tech deep dive (60 min) — confirm Tue 10:30–11:30 PT.
2) Marissa to deliver a technical requirements doc within 48 hours of the call.
3) Mateo to follow with SOW and POC timeline (typical POC 3–6 weeks depending on network readiness).

If you'd like, I can include a sample SOW showing both a Dedicated-with-security-addendum option and the Private VPC option side-by-side to make the procurement comparison easier.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
